title: Permission graph for usage view projections and ad-hoc visibility filters
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce an expressible permission graph and evaluation layer that powers derived usage view projections and supports on-demand visibility filters. Current problems: (1) ad-hoc SQL projections in the console bypass coarse endpoints and leak ephemeral columns, (2) per-route checks are duplicated across microservices, and (3) caching TTLs either over-restrict or over-permit. This ticket defines the graph model, evaluation API, and the migration path to replace inlined row-filter logic with a reusable permission evaluator service.
acceptance_criteria: Permission graph schema documented and validated in Confluence: attributes, edges, and derived roles
A lightweight permission-evaluator service implemented with endpoints: /evaluate and /explain (read-only)
Console usage-views call the evaluator for ad-hoc column visibility and row predicates; no sensitive columns are shown without allow decision
Evaluator response is cacheable with explicit cache keys and TTL; default TTLs and cache-invalidation hooks implemented
Migration demo: port at least two existing usage-view endpoints (per-route /stats and /billing-usage) to use the evaluator behind a feature flag
Security review completed and threat-model notes attached
Benchmark: eval latency <= 3ms p50 for cached checks, <= 12ms p99 for uncached complex policies on our staging hardware
decisions: Use an attribute-based graph (nodes = principals, resources, roles; edges = membership, delegation, attribute assertions) instead of ad-hoc SQL predicates to keep evaluation language deterministic
Keep evaluator stateless; all policy data is read from a sharded policy store with changefeed-driven in-memory indexes to allow low-latency evaluation
Expose an /explain endpoint for debug-mode that returns stringified evaluation steps (no sensitive data) to aid SRE and PM investigations
Default caching: per-principal x resource subset for 10s; config overridable per-route for high-churn endpoints
Fallback policy when policy store is unreachable: conservative-deny to preserve least-privilege
